title: Seat both wing roots on a spar and leave an opening path for a hatch
applicability: Use for a small aircraft with mirrored wing surfaces and a service hatch. Provide matching wing plates, a common spar with a stud row for each root and a paired hinge outside the wing envelope.
steps: Set the centerline and fore–aft stations first. Put both wing roots over the same spar using matching left and right parts. Reserve enough engaged studs at the root for the amount of overhang the wing skin needs.

Place the hatch hinge in a separate station. Give the moving side access to the desired opening angle before adding a canopy lip, fairing or trim. For a thicker skin, allow room near both the hinge and the far edge.

Open the hatch in a posed snapshot and verify that both wings stay fixed. Sample the angle range with the wing surfaces present. For a completed aircraft, also inspect whether the open hatch leaves the intended user access.
expected: The two wings mate to the common spar. The hatch opens upward by 60° without moving either wing and passes seven clearance samples.
